newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi
Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch
for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
HOME MINISTRY MOVES TO REIN IN STATE GOVERNOR

The home minister moved decisively to halt governor Romesh Bhandari's rule in Uttar Pradesh. He initiated a series of measures aimed at directly monitoring the state's law and order apparatus. An action plan was prepared to smash criminal groups operating in the state. Consequently, top Uttar Pradesh administrative and police officials were summoned to the home ministry.
The Economic Times
RADICAL INCOME TAX REFORMS TO BOOST INVESTMENTS

Lower taxes but tighter compliance was proposed by the expert panel constituted to recommend changes in the income tax structure. The new tax regime would serve the twin objectives of simplifying the procedures while widening the tax base. The panel proposed radical reforms in areas of capital gains tax on financial and non-financial assets, taxing of salaries, tax exemption on savings, treatment of income from export sales, depreciation rates and a range of allowable business and professional expenses.
DAEWOO, PAL PEUGEOT SLIP ON EXPORT CLAUSE

Export obligations of foreign car manufacturers who have set up shop in the country would soon be reviewed. Commerce Ministry officials said there were no exports from these car manufacturers to date as stipulated in the agreement signed with the government. Officials said DCM Daewoo and PAL-Peugeot failed to meet export obligations for this year. Other companies such as Mercedes Benz, General Motors, Fiat and Ford would start exporting only from the next financial year.
Financial Express
RELIANCE CONSULTANCY'S SUSPENSION TAKES EFFECT

The Finance Ministry upheld the bourse regulator's decision to suspend Reliance Consultancy Services (RCS), the registrar of Reliance group companies, from carrying out share transfer activities for six months. Following the decision, share transfer activity of Reliance Industries and Reliance Petroleum would be done by these two companies themselves.
FOREIGN EXCHANGE REMITTANCE NORMS EASED

The foreign exchange remittance procedure was relaxed for certain categories of trading houses, export houses and state-owned companies. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) allowed these firms to make overseas remittances without routing documents compulsorily through banking channels. However, other procedural requirements would continue to be effective.
JAPANESE VENTURE CAPITAL GIANT PLANS INDIAN FORAY

Japan Asia Investment Company (JAIC), the $1 billion venture capital company, would enter India, making it the first Japanese company to offer venture capital in the country. JAIC has tied up with a rapidly expanding financial services company, STI Finance, belonging to the Indore-based Steel Tubes of India group. JAIC would initially take a 20 percent stake in STI Finance and help the company expand its network and business in retail financial services.
UNION SWITCH SETS UP OFFICE IN INDIA

Union Switch and Signal (US&S), a world leader in the design and manufacture of railway signalling and control equipment, set up office in India. Although US&S has received in principle clearance to set up a 100 percent owned subsidiary, it was yet to receive a formal communication about the same. Company sources said the Indian unit was planning an investment of around $4 billion.
BUDGET MAKES INDIA MORE INVESTOR-FRIENDLY, SAYS U.S.

The U.S. Department of Commerce expected discussions with Indian trade representative to end on a positive note, following duty reductions announced in the 1997/98 budget, the assistant secretary at the Department of Commerce said. He said the U.S. welcomed many positive aspects of the budget such as the lowering of tax rates, reduction of import duties, partial opening up of the insurance sector and special incentives for the telecommunications sector.
Business Standard
APEX BANK TO STERILISE INTERVENTION EFFECTS

The Reserve Bank of India will offload government securities in its portfolio in the market and siphon off rupee funds in the procedure. This was imperative to negate the effects of its recent intervention in the foreign exchange markets to stop the rupee from appreciating against the dollar.
INDIA READY FOR FULL FLOAT OF RUPEE

India was ready for capital account convertibility and could initiate steps in this direction in the next few months, the International Monetary Fund managing director said. He said the country was strong in the basic preconditions required for full convertibility of the rupee on balance of payments. He urged the government to pursue the next phase of structural reforms and engage in further consolidation of public finances.
CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRY FEARS DECLINE IN GROWTH RATE

The capital goods industry expects sharp deceleration in growth in 1997/98 (April-March) due to the changes in the duty structure for inputs. The growth rate in the current fiscal year was 16.6 percent. The industry opposes the reduction in import duty on capital goods to 20 percent from 25 percent when the duty on steel was left above 20 percent. This resulted in a higher cost of domestically producing capital goods using imported steel than the landed cost of imported capital goods.
The Observer
HINDUJA POWER PROJECT GOES TO CABINET PANEL

The cabinet deferred a decision on a 1,040-megawatt power project being built by the Hindujas at Vizag due to variations in the power purchase agreement and differences between the coal and power ministries over the fuel supply pact. The cabinet discussed the power ministry's recommendation on the fuel supply and transportation agreement for the project.
CRUDE BASIC PRICE, ROYALTY UP

The basic price and royalty of indigenous crude produced by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India (OIL) has been increased. The hike will be effective from April 1996. The move was part of the government's plan to give international prices to crude oil produced by ONGC and OIL, experts said.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX TOUCHES 4029.56

The Bombay bourse index crossed the 4,000-mark in intra-day trading but could not hold at these levels as profit-taking pushed down prices sharply. Reflecting the trend, the sensitive index opened higher at 3965.03, shot up to a high of 4029.56, and shed the gains to close the session with a loss of 3.62 points at 3940.99.
